title: Empty desert produces a similar score distribution
question: Is the output any different when there is no pyramid at all?
finding: The mean best score is 0.306 on the pyramid footprint and 0.306 in the desert-only scene. Their empirical distribution distance is 0.0096. The absence of buried objects does not prevent structured output.
limitations: One realization per scene; the 32-pixel patches overlap on a 4-pixel grid, so the samples are dependent. The saved conventional KS p-value is descriptive only here. Similar distributions do not establish statistical equivalence or validate a detector.
method: Identical pipeline and grid as T1 on a scene containing only clutter and sparse rocks; scores compared pixel by pixel with T1's pyramid footprint.

Same scale, two scenes. Best-fit score maps for a pyramid scene and a desert-only scene. Both inputs contain no buried objects. This comparison tests this score's specificity, rather than proving the two scenes identical.
